Steve Irwin was born in Australia in 1962. Ever since he was young, he had a fascination with nature, especially dangerous animals.
His father, a famous herpetologist , encouraged his son's hobby. Steve received a 4-meter-long snake when he was six and began wrestling crocodiles when he was nine.

As a teenager, Irwin got a job capturing crocodiles that turned up in people's yards. Some of these were released into the wild; he brought the rest to a holding pen, which eventually became the Australia Zoo.
People heard about Irwin's exciting antics. In 1996, Australian TV began a show about him called "The Crocodile Hunter."
Soon, the show came to the USA, and Irwin became famous around the world. He used the money to grow the zoo and promote conservation.
Irwin traveled the world with his TV show. Australians loved him for bringing tourists to their country.
In 2006, he went to the Great Barrier Reef to film stingrays. In a freak accident, a ray stung him, and he died. He left behind a wife and two children.
Many people praised his work educating people about animals, his support for conservation, and his passion and respect for wildlife.
However, some animal rights activists criticized Irwin's style. They said he was wrong to touch and grab wild animals, and that the right way to study nature is to look at it — not touch it.
Steve Irwin began wrestling crocodiles when he was fifteen.

Mary Donaldson was born in 1972 in Hobart, Australia. Growing up, she lived a pretty normal life with her family. Her father was a mathematician and university professor, while her mother worked as an office assistant. She was the youngest of four children.
Mary's family also spent several years in the USA. Mary was a very smart girl and finished high school early.
Then, she attended the University of Tasmania in Australia, studying business and law. After she graduated, she started a successful career as a businesswoman.
Everything changed one evening in 2000 in Sydney. Mary met a young, handsome man from Denmark. He was in Australia for the Summer Olympics. He said his name was "Fred."
Mary and Fred hit it off and started dating.
Who was "Fred," really?
After Fred went home, they exchanged e-mails and talked on the phone. Fred flew back to Australia several times to see her.
Later, she learned that her boyfriend was actually Prince Frederik, the Crown Prince of Denmark!
Mary moved to Europe to be close to Frederik. In 2001, she taught English in France. A few months later, she moved to Denmark.
In 2003, Frederik's mother, Queen Margrethe II, announced that they could get married. They were married in 2004.
Years later, they are still happily married with four children. As Princess of Denmark, Mary attended many events and did charity work.
In January 2024, Queen Margrethe stepped down, and Frederik became King of Denmark. Mary became Queen!
Mary never imagined she would become a princess. She worked very hard. She learned Danish, a very difficult language, and studied Danish history, culture, and royal manners.
Today she is fluent in Danish. Most Danes think she does a good job.

The blues is a genre of African American folk music that is the basis for much of modern American popular music. Indeed, it was first developed in the United States and influenced all later popular music styles, including jazz and rock and roll.
From the 1600s, millions of Africans were taken to North America as slaves. Life was terrible, and music was one of their few escapes.
In the fields, they sang work songs with call and response: one person sang, and everyone answered.
Since they didn't have any instruments, the slaves banged shovels and other tools to make the rhythm. Because of their hard lives, most of the songs were sad and forlorn.
The melodies used notes called "blue notes." This is how the blues got its name!
The slaves played guitars to make the rhythm.
Slavery in the USA ended in 1865, after the Civil War. Then African Americans were free to make their own music. Musicians traveled the country in road shows.
Now the songs had instruments: the piano, horns, and later the guitar. Drums and bass kept the rhythm.
[BTS 34 (007 - 009) Music] New / Slide2: In the mid-1900s, radio and records made the blues even more popular. It had a huge influence on rock and roll.
Today, big and small bands play the blues everywhere. Cities like Chicago and Memphis are proud of their blues heritage.

Today, Choi Sung Bong is famous around Korea and the world as a classical opera singer. When he sang on "Korea's Got Talent" in 2011, his beautiful singing moved the audience and even the judges to tears. The video became an internet sensation around the world.
Back then, no one knew his amazing story or how he got there. Choi was born in 1990. He lived in an orphanage, ran away at five, and lived on the street.
He made a living selling candy and soda. He never went to school, and he often slept in stairwells.

Despite his very difficult situation, Choi had an amazing dream. When he was 14, he was selling gum at a nightclub when he heard a beautiful opera song. After that, he knew he wanted to be an opera singer.
Choi was determined to succeed in music. He usually didn't have enough money for music lessons. Instead, he taught himself.

Choi never gave up on his dream. He never attended middle school, but he worked hard to get a GED certificate. Then he attended Daejeon Arts High School, although he had to work as a laborer at night.
His life finally changed in 2011, when the world heard his amazing voice. Today, he doesn't have to sleep outside anymore.
Choi's story was moving and inspiring to millions of people. The international media compared his story to that of Susan Boyle, a Scottish woman with a similar story.
Their success stories can inspire other people to follow their dreams and live up to their potential. Every person has potential for greatness.
